## How they got there
Liverpool reached the final as runners-up after losing to Real Madrid 0-1 in the decisive match. Their campaign was defined by a dominant profile featuring a points per game average of 3.0, where they performed better than 97% of teams in that season's group and league phase, alongside shot accuracy at 59.2% which beat 97% of their peers in the same period. The squad also controlled possession at 59.5%, a metric superior to 97% of teams during the group and league stages.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Liverpool, ranking them second among all knockout teams with a probability of 32.5% for reaching the final. This likelihood is significantly higher than the base rate of 12.5%, which represents the chance a random knockout team reaches the final. Consequently, the stage nearest to the model's expectation of 2.24 on its scale is the semi-finals, placing them well inside the top two predictions despite the actual outcome being the final.

## Weak spots
The analysis identifies distance covered per game as a lower-performing area, with Liverpool recording 113.1 km and beating only 25% of teams in that season's group or league phase. Their foul count was also relatively high compared to peers, committing an average of 12.0 fouls per game which placed them ahead of just 38% of the season's competitors. Additionally, long passes accounted for 13.1% of their total passing, a figure that outperformed only 47% of teams during the group and league phases.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Teams beaten (%)' figures say how many teams the club did better than on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where doing better means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
